shortDescription: German day-ahead power prices fell nearly 9% on Thursday as cooling weather was expected to lead to easing consumption.($1 = 0.8713 euros)

children: German day-ahead power prices fell nearly 9% on Thursday as cooling weather was expected to lead to easing consumption.
The German baseload spot electricity contract (TRDEBD1) fell 8.6% to €128.30 ($147.25) per megawatt hour at 0747 GMT, according to LSEG data.

"Temperatures are now moving closer to seasonal averages, with cooling demand very low and no meaningful heating demand yet. Wind conditions are also very favourable today, particularly in Germany," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote in a note.
While wind and solar power generation are expected to increase by a combined 1.2 gigawatts, consumption in Germany is expected to fall by 1 GW to 54.4 GW.
The French equivalent contract (TRFRBD1) fell 1.1% to €131.50/MWh, the data showed.
Consumption in France is set to edge 0.5 GW lower, while wind power generation is expected to fall by 2.5 GW and solar power generation is seen largely stable at 4.9 GW.
French nuclear availability was flat at 80% of total capacity.
Along the curve, the German 2027 baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) tracked gas prices to fall 1.5% to €127.10/MWh.
The French equivalent contract (TRFRBYc1) was down 2.1% to €85.30/MWh, the data showed.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was largely stable at €84.74 a metric ton.
